chapter: Billy Bauer, George Russell and Charlie Parker
title: Knowing Charlie Parker on the Kenton tour
summary: Parker was friendly to Konitz on tour and a story about him in a music store; Bird hugging a propeller in a photo.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: How well did you know him?
Not really well but every time we met it was very friendly. We hung out once when we were doing guests on the Stan Kenton tour.

Yeah. He was very kind. My wife was having a baby soon and he came over to hang out: “You need a friend?”, you know. [He] took me to his hotel, we had lunch together in the room. I don’t know that we spoke a dozen words…he always said that he appreciated that I didn’t play like him and I think he meant that. The fact that I couldn’t was beside the point. [Laughs] “Its too hard” I said.
At least you had an alternative worked out. I don’t think I’ve ever heard anybody who knew him say they ever had a discussion about equipment or talking shop. He wasn’t into that.
The only thing I heard about was that he and Sonny Stitt went to Santi Runyon, the man I was taking lessons from later. I was with him once and we went
into a music store in some city and he asked for a particular book and then tried to get it for nothing, telling them he was Charlie Parker.
There’s that one picture in your book of you and Bird hugging the propeller.
I look like I was just Bar Mitsvahed and he looks like he’s just going out to lunch.
